headline: Interpretable multi-omics methods link transcriptomic and metabolomic data to function
label: Interpretable Multi Omics Network Inference
summary: Four preprints pair interpretable inference with network or multi-omic data to predict tissue glycan potential, protein function, and regulatory metabolites.
synthesis: The common thread is interpretable inference over biological networks or paired omic layers, with outputs tied to explicit mechanistic structure. Glycan reachability analysis scores tissue glycan biosynthetic potential from GTEx RNA-seq using AND/OR logic and minimum bottleneck scoring. MAAMOUL maps disease-association scores from paired metagenomic and metabolomic data onto a microbiome metabolic network. Lemonite targets regulatory metabolites through data-driven integration of transcriptomics and metabolomics, explicitly addressing limits in interpretability and incomplete prior knowledge. VaLPAS applies correlation and autoencoder methods to multi-omic variation for guilt-by-association prediction of protein and gene function. The dominant thread is attribution through explicit structure rather than opaque prediction. What is new is the combination of cross-omic integration with explicit network logic, although the four methods differ in input data and inference target.
